newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Huge block sales of Astra shares reported.
newsitem.headline: Huge block sales of Astra shares reported.

text.p: Indonesia's small stock exchange in the city of Surabaya said on Friday that huge block sales of shares in Astra International have been recorded, involving about a 14 percent stake in the automobile company.
An exchange statement said 144 million Astra shares were sold on the Surabaya exchange on Thursday with the value of the deals reaching 603.4 trillion rupiah.

The statement did not identify any buyers or sellers but Bisnis Indonesia newspaper said a group linked to Presaident Suharto had purchased the shares from state-owned banks and pension funds and from tobacco tycoon Putera Sampoerna.

The buyer, the Nusamba group, is 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by Suharto with the rest of the holdings divided between the president's eldest son and timber tycoon Muhamad "Bob" Hasan.
Hasan, who heads Nusamba, was not available for comment. Aides said he was out of the country and that they had no comment on the newspaper report.
Bisnis Indonesia said Nusamba bought 20 million shares from Sampoerna, the head of cigarette company PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna, and the rest from state institutions.
It also said Nusamba had picked up a 2.85 percent stake in Astra earlier in the week from a subsidiary of PT Sampoerna.
That would imply that Nusamba now owns the largest stake in Astra, which is 8.26 percent owned by Toyota Motor corp.

On Wednesday, the government said it wanted to ensure that the holdings in Astra remained widely-held, and senior officials privately said that Nusamba's activities were aimed at blocking Sampoerna from a possible takeover of the company.
Astra closed at 4,000 rupiah on a volume of 4.7 million shares on the Jakarta exchange on Thursday.
